The quarterly review showed steady growth across every region, although the northern division lagged behind expectations for the second consecutive period. Management attributed the shortfall to supply delays and a slower hiring cycle, and committed to a recovery plan that prioritises logistics partnerships over new product launches. Analysts remained cautiously optimistic: margins held, customer retention improved, and the backlog of unfulfilled orders fell by nearly a third. Still, several board members questioned whether the plan was ambitious enough, noting that competitors had already expanded into adjacent markets with considerable success.
When the team gathered on Friday afternoon, the mood was lighter than anyone expected. Coffee was poured, jokes were made about the projector that never worked, and somebody finally fixed the thermostat. It's remarkable how small comforts change the tone of a difficult conversation.
